generator.params.basal_area.note: The leaf area its `basal` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms Skill 1, 2026-10-14; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: the look now takes its card from the taxa's characters, where before it drew the generic card (0.235); drawn again with the teeth the kingdom's margin rule gives it (2026-10-16).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Piper and Beattie 1915, as Aster douglasii, p. 372: erect stems 30 cm to 120 cm high (Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, 1960, p. 318, as Aster subspicatus, say about 1 m high or less).

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a leafy aster forming patches, with narrow leaves and loose clusters of lavender heads with yellow centres in late summer. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.8 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves; lavender heads.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): slender, about 1 m high or less, with erect or ascending branches.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): perennial (genus: ours mostly perennial herbs).

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): a herb.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): middle leaves 7-13 cm long, 1-2 cm wide.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): middle leaves 1-2 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): middle leaves lanceolate, the lowest oblanceolate narrowed to a winged petiole-like base.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): leaves toothed only.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): lowest leaves serrate, middle ones usually serrate above the middle.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): inflorescence a cymose panicle with few to many heads 2-3 cm wide.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): rays 20-30.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): involucre 5-6 mm high, loosely overlapping, the phyllaries with green herbaceous tips.

traits.ray_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): rays 20-30.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): rays about 1 cm long.

traits.ray_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): rays violet. Word: violet.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Aster subspicatus (pp. 318-319; syn. A. douglasii): June to October.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.involucre.note: The involucre drawn about 0.6 times as tall as the disc is wide, so its height comes to the flora's 5 to 6 mm (spec rework E1); the daisy family's rule sets it from the involucre's height and width, and no flora read gives this aster's width.
